subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderately detailed static vehicle model with around 150+ parts and several textures, keeping it simple by skipping joints and relying on part, extrude, lathe, and glow functions, along with the usual builder imports.

I'm sketching the layout of a six-wheel hauler facing forward with a cab at the front and a cargo flatbed at the rear, working out the chassis dimensions, wheel placement across three axles, and the cab's sloped windshield profile using extruded shapes.

Computing the windshield's normal direction and sizing it to fit the slope, then placing side window planes with textured grid overlays, and adding grille and headlight details to the front of the hood.

Now I'm adding exterior accessories: bull bar rods, a magenta roof light bar, antennas, and twin exhaust stacks behind the cab. I'm planning to use merged geometries for the rivets and bolts on the armor side skirts to keep things efficient, and setting up a lathe-based cargo pod with a radius and length positioned behind the cab.

Working out the pod's octagonal profile and placement, then adding thin lathe rings around the pod at intervals to create raised banding details.

Still placing pod details and seal strip geometry... now working out the cradle saddle blocks, straps, and chassis frame with pocketed wheel fenders and cylinder wheels.

Designing wheel details...

I'll build the tread and lug geometry locally with mirrored placement per side, then add fender arches over each wheel pair as simple boxes centered around the axle positions.

Checking height stacking from chassis base through roof, light bar, exhaust, and pod so everything aligns, then adding cab trim: mirrors, door seams, handle, stencil decal, hood vents, armor plates, and front bumper with bull bar rods.

Now adding a winch drum, magenta underglow strips, red tail lights with rear bumper and tow hitch, plus a roof-mounted turret with twin barrels and muzzle brakes on the cab. I'm also planning amber beacon lights and sensor details on the pod, along with textures for the windshield HUD, windows, grille, door numbering, and a neon billboard sign on the cab side.

I'm settling on a "SEALED" decal instead of kanji for the pod, bringing the total texture count to around six including hazard stripes and warning triangles. For the palette I'm going with gunmetal hull, magenta and cyan accents, amber highlights, and a light pod color against hazard yellow, then building custom paint logic with warm-to-cool shading, grime near the base, scratch noise, and paneled seam lines for the pod surface.

I'm setting up box-drawing helpers and a glow wrapper, mirroring parts across both sides, and deciding which textured parts should glow versus stay flat -- windshields stay dark with cyan highlights rather than glowing, while the grille gets glow. I'm also working out the floor contact points, making sure wheel cylinders sit flush at y=0.

Adjusting wheel tread geometry...

Adding lugs, hub, and glow ring details...

Writing seam paint function...

Working out the barrel positions and muzzle glow, then checking that the cab roof placement and windshield height line up with the turret so nothing clips through the windshield across the z-range.

Now I'm placing the exhaust stacks behind the cab, positioning them just outside the pod's radius so they clear the rounded nose, and adding caps, bands, and a heat glow at the tips.

Then I'm fitting the fenders over the wheels, checking the width spans so the wheel sits inside the fender properly, and adding a side mirror with a small cyan glowing face mounted on a rod arm. I'm also laying out magenta underglow boxes along the chassis for a neon effect, and considering adding fuel or battery tanks between the axles on the chassis sides.

Now I'm checking the tank placement — rotating cylinders to lie along the z-axis, positioning them on either side of the chassis between the wheel gaps, and shortening them slightly to avoid colliding with the cab.

I should also add mudflaps and step ladders for detail, then finalize the model.
